---
name: polish-wording
description: Polish grammar and wording for natural English readability while preserving the author's meaning, voice, and structure.
---

Polish the requested prose for fluent, natural English without changing what the
author means. Work only on the text or files the user identifies. If no text or
scope is provided, ask what should be polished rather than guessing.

- Fix grammar, spelling, punctuation, awkward idioms, repetition, and unnatural
  sentence flow.
- Preserve every factual claim, opinion, example, chronology, qualification,
  link, and technical term unless a correction is purely mechanical.
- Retain the author's personality, level of formality, emphasis, and deliberate
  informality. Do not flatten the prose into generic corporate or AI language.
- Do not add new arguments, remove ideas, strengthen claims, introduce facts, or
  reorganize the piece beyond what readability requires.
- Leave code, commands, frontmatter values, citations, URLs, and other
  non-prose content unchanged unless the user explicitly includes them.
- Prefer the smallest revision that reads naturally to a fluent English reader.

After editing, review the diff sentence by sentence for semantic drift and undo
any unnecessary rewrite. Run applicable formatting, content, or build checks,
and summarize the scope polished without claiming that the underlying facts
were verified.
